title: Show how long a bed has been sitting empty since its last tenant, not just gaps between two tenants
description:
Filed from UAT on LODGY-93. The bed sheet's past-occupants list (built in LODGY-93) shows vacant stretches BETWEEN two recorded tenancies, per that ticket's design - and that part works exactly as intended. But the single most common version of 'why does this bed keep sitting empty' - the case DESIGN.md and LODGY-91/93 both cite as the whole reason this feature exists - is a bed whose LAST occupant checked out some time ago and nobody has moved in since. That trailing stretch, from the last checkout to today, is not shown anywhere on the sheet. A warden sees 'Past occupants: Ramesh Kumar, 1 Jun 2023 - 31 Dec 2023' and has to do the date subtraction themselves against today's date to realize the bed has been empty for two and a half years - the app has all the information needed to say that plainly and doesn't.

This is not a defect in LODGY-93: its acceptance criteria explicitly scope vacant stretches to 'between occupancies', and a bed with nothing after its last tenant has no 'next occupancy' to bound the gap against. This is a real, additive gap the ticket didn't promise to close.

Worth noting there is already a proactive notification for this (LODGY-59's long-vacant-bed nudge) - this ticket is not about alerting the warden, it's about the bed sheet itself telling the truth plainly when the warden is already looking at it, the same way it already does for gaps between two tenants.
acceptanceCriteria: A bed whose most recent occupancy has ended, with nobody currently in it, shows how long it has been vacant since that checkout - in the same plain style as the existing between-tenancies gap rows, not just the checkout date on its own
A bed that has never been occupied still says 'Never occupied' as today - this only applies once there is at least one closed period to measure from
A bed whose most recent period is still open (currently occupied) is unaffected - no vacancy line is shown for it
Correct for a shop, warehouse or flat, consistent with the rest of LODGY-93's history rows carrying no room/bed label
Correct in Hindi as well as English

history.note: Filed while doing UAT on LODGY-91/92/93/94. Noticed on Room 101 Bed A, which has been vacant since a backfilled tenant's checkout on 31 Dec 2023 (today is 17 Sep 2026, so nearly three years) - the sheet shows the checkout date but nothing that reads as 'this has been empty a long time', which is exactly the question that ticket set out to answer. Priority Low since LODGY-59 already covers the proactive-alert half of this need; this is the passive, look-it-up-yourself half.

Starting. bedHistoryEntries() (app/src/main/java/com/lodgy/app/ui/property/BedHistory.kt) only computes gaps BETWEEN two occupied periods; a bed whose most recent period is closed with nothing after it gets no trailing entry at all.

Built: bedHistoryEntries and pastOccupancyEntries both take a nowMillis parameter (defaulting to System.currentTimeMillis(), overridable in tests for determinism). When the chronologically last period is closed (bed currently vacant) and nowMillis is after its endDate, a trailing Vacant(lastEnd, nowMillis) entry is appended - reusing the exact same BedHistoryEntry.Vacant type and the existing bed_history_vacant string, so BedGridScreen needed zero changes: it already renders any Vacant entry generically. A still-open period (bed currently occupied) never gets one, and a bed with no periods at all is unaffected (still short-circuits to "Never occupied" before this code runs). No new strings, so Hindi is free - same string, same DurationLabel. Docs: DESIGN.md 4.3 + decision log. Unit tests: BedHistoryTest extended with the trailing-vacancy case, the still-open guard, and pastOccupancyEntries ordering (the trailing stretch sorts to the top, above older history, since it is the most recent state); one pre-existing test pinned nowMillis to its last endDate so it stays focused on the between-tenancies gap it was already testing. 634 tests pass, 0 failures, line coverage 95.72% (gate 0.93), assembleDebug succeeds. Not yet verified on device.

FAIL - real regression, found while testing AC3 ("a bed whose most recent period is still open (currently occupied) is unaffected"). bedHistoryEntries infers "is this bed currently vacant" from whether the chronologically LAST occupancy_period is closed - but that is not reliable. Room 102 Bed A is genuinely OCCUPIED right now (beds.status=OCCUPIED, Ramesh Kumar's tenancy is ACTIVE there) - but his tenancy predates occupancy-period tracking and has never been transferred, so it has ZERO occupancy_periods of its own. The bed does have one older, unrelated CLOSED backfilled period (Test Kumar, 1 Jan - 1 Feb 2024). Because that closed period is the only one on record and therefore chronologically "last", the new trailing-vacancy logic fires and the sheet reads "Vacant for 2 year(s) 7 month(s)" directly above "Occupied by Ramesh Kumar" - actively wrong, not just unhelpful. This is exactly the same class of bug as the one just fixed on LODGY-92/94 (inferring real-world state from occupancy_periods alone, when a pre-existing/untransferred tenancy has none) - it will hit every currently-occupied bed that also has any older recorded history once one of the beds involved predates this feature, which for an existing warden is common. Root cause: bedHistoryEntries/pastOccupancyEntries have no signal for "is this bed ACTUALLY occupied right now" independent of the periods list - they need one (bed.status, or the same tenantId != null check the sheet already uses for "Occupied by X") and must suppress the trailing entry whenever it is OCCUPIED, regardless of what the last period's endDate says. IMPORTANT: this shares the exact function LODGY-93 (already Delivered) depends on for its own past-occupants list - LODGY-93 itself did not have this bug before this change (it never inferred vacancy, only ever filtered a still-open period), so this is a regression introduced by this ticket's own code, not a pre-existing LODGY-93 defect. Fixing this restores correctness for both. AC1 (trailing vacancy on a genuinely vacant bed, verified on Room 101 Bed A: "Vacant for 2 year(s) 8 month(s)" correctly shown) and the never-occupied-bed guard (untouched, separate code path) are fine - only the occupied-bed case is broken.

Fixed the regression the Tester found. bedHistoryEntries and pastOccupancyEntries (app/src/main/java/com/lodgy/app/ui/property/BedHistory.kt) now take an explicit currentlyOccupied: Boolean instead of inferring vacancy from whether the last period is closed. pastOccupancyEntries computes it from the authoritative source - selectedBed.bed.status == BedStatus.OCCUPIED - not from the periods list, so a bed occupied by an untracked pre-existing tenancy with an older unrelated closed period on file no longer reads as vacant. New tests: the exact regression case (occupied bed, one closed unrelated period, no trailing entry) at both the pastOccupancyEntries level and the bedHistoryEntries level directly. 636 tests pass (2 new), 0 failures, line coverage 95.72% (gate 0.93), assembleDebug succeeds. Docs: DESIGN.md 4.3 + decision log updated with the corrected reasoning. Please re-verify on Room 102 Bed A specifically (the exact bed that showed the false reading) alongside the two cases already passed (Room 101 Bed A genuinely vacant, and the never-occupied guard).

PASS - re-verified on the exact bed that regressed. Room 102 Bed A (Ramesh Kumar, ACTIVE tenancy with no occupancy_period of its own, plus Test Kumar's older unrelated closed backfilled period) now correctly shows only "Occupied by Ramesh Kumar" and "Past occupants: Test Kumar, 1 Jan 2024 - 1 Feb 2024" - the false "Vacant for 2 year(s) 7 month(s)" line is gone. Re-confirmed the genuinely-vacant case still works: Room 101 Bed A still shows "Vacant for 2 year(s) 8 month(s)" above Ramesh's backfilled stay there. The never-occupied guard is a separate, untouched early-return path (bedHistory.isEmpty() check happens before any of the changed logic runs), so not re-driven through the UI this pass. All of LODGY-95's acceptance criteria hold now, including AC3 which is what exposed the regression.

Accepted. Room 101 Bed A tells me plainly it has been vacant for 2 year(s) 8 month(s) - I do not have to subtract the checkout date from today myself, and "Assign a tenant" is right there on the same sheet once I see it. Just as important: Room 102 Bed A, which is genuinely occupied by Ramesh Kumar right now, does NOT get a false vacancy line even though it also has an old, unrelated backfilled stay on file - I checked this specifically since I would stop trusting this screen the first time it told me an occupied bed was empty.
